title: Bible Guide
paragraph: Kings never names the man of God; it calls him only “a man of God out of Judah”. 1 Kings 13:1

blocks.text: IDDO THE SEER, KNOWN ONLY AS A WRITER · UNITED KINGDOM
Iddo. Named three times in Chronicles, always as the author of a record.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Seer
ERA
United kingdom c. 1050–930 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Solomon · Jeroboam I · Rehoboam · Abijah
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
Chronicles calls him “the seer” twice and “the prophet” once, and names three records: “visions”, a book “concerning genealogies”, and a “story”.
THE CALL
How the word came

Chronicles calls him “the seer” twice and “the prophet” once, and names three records: “visions”, a book “concerning genealogies”, and a “story”. 2 Chronicles 9:29 2 Chronicles 12:15 2 Chronicles 13:22
Scholars' viewThe word rendered “story” is the Hebrew midrash; W. E. Barnes notes that the Revised Version renders it “commentary”. 2 Chronicles 13:22 [12][107]
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before four kings
KING OF ALL ISRAEL
Solomon
KING OF ISRAEL
Jeroboam I
KING OF JUDAH
Rehoboam
KING OF JUDAH
Abijah
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Shemaiah the prophet
Nathan and Ahijah
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture says nothing of Iddo's life or death. 2 Chronicles 13:22
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Scripture's account
The text of 1 Kings 13
Kings never names the man of God; it calls him only “a man of God out of Judah”. 1 Kings 13:1
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 3
2 Chronicles 9 2 Chronicles 12 2 Chronicles 13
PASSAGES · 3
2 Chronicles 9:29 2 Chronicles 12:15 2 Chronicles 13:22
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
No word Iddo spoke is recorded; Chronicles names only his writings.
Scripture gives no father or home for him.
He is a different man from the Iddo named as the prophet Zechariah's grandfather after the exile (Zechariah 1:1; Ezra 5:1).
